newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka rupee ends weaker on trade demand for dlrs.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka rupee ends weaker on trade demand for dlrs.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed weaker against the dollar on Tuesday due to commercial demand for the U.S. unit, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.77 to the dollar, after opening at 58.74 and falling to a low of 58.80, they said. The rupee closed at 58.72 on Monday.
"The rupee fell to 58.80 on trade-backed demand for the dollar, at which level selling came in," said a Hongkong Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by four local cents, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.6575 and 59.8425.
"Given the continuing overseas strength of the dollar and local trade-backed demand, the rupee could touch 58.90 in the coming week," said the Hongkong Bank dealer.
Overnight call money closed at 9.875 percent after touching 10.25, due to a slight tightness in the market, dealers said.
"Lending banks have tied up money in one and two week repos, creating a temporary tightness," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
